short_description: Laptop drops off home Wi-Fi every 10-15 minutes
description: Working from home on a consumer router. Roughly every 10-15 minutes my laptop loses the wireless connection, then reconnects by itself a minute later. It is wrecking my calls. Phone on the same Wi-Fi seems fine.
expected_answer:
1. Restart the PC first. [Article: KB0010174]
2. Have the device forget the Wi-Fi network, then reconnect from scratch. [Article: KB0010174]
3. Restart the router to clear temporary glitches causing repeated drops. [Article: KB0010174]
4. As a remote worker on a consumer router, check for signal interference or an overloaded connection. [Article: KB0010174]

provenance.derivation: Symptom (periodic drops, home worker, consumer router) written from scratch; maps to the restart / forget-network / restart-router / remote-worker-interference bullets. Title words ('keeps disconnecting') deliberately not reused.

short_description: Pages crawl although Wi-Fi shows full bars
description: Connection never drops, but websites take ages to load and a speed test gives about 4 Mbps while our plan is 50 Mbps. Happens on the laptop and the desktop.
expected_answer:
1. Restart the PC, then run a speed test and compare it to the plan's expected speed. [Article: KB0010171]
2. Restart the router and modem to clear temporary network issues. [Article: KB0010171]
3. Check Wi-Fi signal strength; move closer to the router, reposition the access point, or use a wired connection. [Article: KB0010171]
4. For remote workers, test the modem and check for ISP outages; escalate to the ISP if it persists. [Article: KB0010171]

provenance.derivation: Built from the speed-test-vs-plan bullet; deliberately says the connection does NOT drop so Wi-Fi Keeps Disconnecting (KB0010174) is a hard negative.

short_description: Downloads crawl and Teams lags only when I am on the company VPN
description: From the home network everything is quick. The moment I connect to the corporate VPN, file downloads crawl and Teams video stutters. Disconnecting the VPN fixes it immediately.
expected_answer:
1. Check the base internet speed outside the VPN to isolate the bottleneck. [Article: KB0010172]
2. Connect to a VPN server location closer to you. [Article: KB0010172]
3. Try switching VPN protocols if the client supports more than one. [Article: KB0010172]
4. Escalate to network admins if performance stays poor across servers and protocols. [Article: KB0010172]

provenance.derivation: Scenario isolates the VPN as the variable (fast without it), matching the 'check base speed outside the VPN' bullet; slow-internet article is the confusable.

3. Re-map the printer or reselect the correct device in the print dialog if the configuration looks off. [Article: KB0010155]

provenance.derivation: Root cause hinted only indirectly (different network) so retrieval must connect it to the 'both devices on the same Wi-Fi network' bullet.
